text: In the Schubert decomposition $G/B = \bigsqcup_{w \in W} C_w$ of the flag variety, each cell is an affine space $C_w \cong \mathbb{A}^d$. The dimension $d$ equals:
choices: $\ell(w)$, the length of $w$ in the Weyl group
$|W|$, the order of the Weyl group
explanation: The chapter gives $C_w \cong \mathbb{A}^{\ell(w)}$, so the cell's dimension is the Coxeter length $\ell(w)$. $|W|$ counts the cells, not the dimension of one cell; the cells have varying dimensions (not all $1$); and $\dim G$ is far larger than $\dim G/B$.
